newsitem.title: FRANCE: France steps up drive for peace in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: France steps up drive for peace in Zaire.

text.p: France on Wednesday hailed hopeful signs of progress toward peace talks on eastern Zaire and said it would step up its own campaign for an end to hostilities between government forces and rebels led by Laurent Kabila.

"A truce or ceasefire is urgently needed," a Foreign Ministry spokesman said, adding that France would be pressing "at the highest levels" in coming days for moves toward peace in the troubled region.

The Foreign Ministry said U.N. special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun as well as United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan would both be in Paris later in the week. "The Zairean crisis will have an important place in all these meetings," spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said.

Kabila said after meeting South African President Nelson Mandela in Johannesburg on Wednesday that he hoped direct negotations could begin soon on a deal for peace in eastern Zaire, where his forces are occupying a large swathe of land.
Also in South Africa to meet Kabila were U.S. Assistant Secretary of State George Moose and U.N. special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun.

Mandela also hopes to soon meet Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, who has ruled the central African state for 31 years but whose ragged army is faring badly against the rebellion, which began in October.
In another diplomatic step, African foreign affairs ministers in Tripoli said they would hold an urgent summit on the situation in Central Africa on March 18-19 in an as-yet-undecided location.

French and Belgian diplomats have in the past expressed fears Washington was intruding on their traditional turf in becoming involved in the search for peace in a region long dominated by Paris and Brussels.
But the French Foreign Ministry noted U.S. involvement with apparent approval on Wednesday.
"We renew our strong support for Mr Sahnoun's peace plan and his mediation efforts in search of peace in the Great Lakes region," Rummelhardt said.
"It is within this framework that the South African initiative is taking place, in which the United States is participating and which seeks even indirect contacts between the parties," he said.
"This initiative is a step in the right direction, We hope it will quickly yield concrete results," Rummelhardt said.
